title: Snowshoe Hares Crash Every 10 Years, and Lynx Are Only Part of Why

scenes.text: Every ten years, snowshoe hares crash across northern Canada. Lynx are only part of why.
Hare numbers swing in a ten-year cycle, rising and then collapsing across the northern forest.
Lynx follow the swing. When hares crash, lynx starve or move away.
But a lynx hunt only succeeds fifteen to twenty percent of the time.
Scientists in the Yukon found it takes both food shortage and fear. Stressed mothers have fewer young.
Not just hunger, not just predators. Both together, every ten years.

description:
Every ten years, snowshoe hares crash across northern Canada, and lynx are only part of why.
Research in Canada's Yukon found that a food shortage and fear of predators together drive the cycle.
Which would you rather track in the wild, a lynx or a hare? Comment below.
first_comment: Lynx crash after the hares do. What do you think happens to the forest in between?
